caption: A dental drill is switched on and held up, and its tip becomes a blur.

sa.check: A dental drill is held up.
The tip is sharp before the switch-on.
The switch-on comes first and the blur follows.

pc.expect: The blur is at the tip only; the handpiece stays sharp and the blur does not appear before the switch.
pc.fail: The tip blurs before the switch; or the whole handpiece blurs while the hand holding it is sharp; or the tip wanders about on its own away from the handpiece.

pc.expect: Once on, the tip blurs and stays blurred while the drill runs; once off, it is sharp.
pc.fail: The switch is pressed and the tip stays sharp for the rest of the clip; or the drill is switched off and the blur remains unchanged; or the blur flickers on and off while nothing at the switch changes.

pc.expect: The handpiece is rigid and the tip stays attached and straight.
pc.fail: The handpiece bends; or the tip stretches longer; or the tip flops like rubber.

pc.expect: A hose or cord attached to the drill hangs downward from it.
pc.fail: The hose arcs upward and stays; or floats; or hangs rigid sideways.
pc.precondition: A hose or cord is attached to the drill.

pc.expect: One drill with one tip; nothing duplicates or vanishes.
pc.fail: The tip vanishes; or a second drill appears; or the tip passes through the handpiece; or the drill turns into another object.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The handpiece's colour, the tip's shape when still and the background stay the same.
pc.fail: The handpiece changes colour; or the background changes; or the tip changes shape when still.

note: The hand holding the drill is a trigger and is not judged.
